title: bjt
description: BJT (npn or pnp) component data. The presence of the 'bjt' field at the top level of an SAS document discriminates the device type — there is no deviceType property.

substitutesInfo.description: Replacement parts for this one: manufacturer-named successors and second sources. An entry with type 'successor' means THIS part is superseded by the named one, one hop, as the manufacturer states it - never inferred from a status of obsolete or from part-number similarity. The schema cannot check that the named part exists in the catalogue, or exists exactly once; that is the referential pass's job, as for CIAS component URIs. Evidence for the claim goes in the record's provenance[] with fields: ["substitutesInfo"], carrying the same sourceUrl, retrievedDate and verification stamp as any datasheet field.

spiceModel.description: Device-body SPICE .model card for a simulation-sourced part (no datasheet). Faithful home that does not require manufacturerInfo.

datasheetInfo.title: bjtDatasheetInfo
datasheetInfo.description: All information extracted from the BJT datasheet.

allOf.$comment: Device-specific narrowing of the shared part def: subType must come from this closed enum (protects the exact-string conditionals, e.g. diode zener/tvs/esd required sets).

dies.description: One entry per transistor die in a multi-die package. Present INSTEAD OF the package-level electrical block, never beside it: a dual has no single V_CEO or h_FE, and a complementary pair has no single polarity. Required when part.dieConfiguration is dual, complementary or array. Order carries no meaning; die are identified by name.

matching.description: Matching specifications between die (matched pairs and quads, current mirrors). Only legal on a part described per die.

packagePowerDissipation.description: Total power dissipation of the PACKAGE with all die conducting (P_tot 'per device' / 'per package'), in W, as the datasheet prints it. Legal only beside dies[]: on a single-die part the package figure is electrical.powerDissipation. The per-transistor rating stays in each die's electrical.powerDissipation; the package total is never divided down to fill it, and a per-die figure is never summed up to fill this one.

allOf.$comment: Matching relates die; it has nothing to attach to on a single-die record.
A complementary pair has no package polarity: part.subType would have to be one die's polarity written as the part's.
A package total relates die; a single-die record states its dissipation in electrical.powerDissipation.

A package that declares two or more die must describe them per die, as on mosfet.json. With electrical XOR dies, this also leaves no package-level electrical block in which one die's numbers (V_CEO, h_FE, bias resistors) could be written as the part's.

voltageNoiseDensity.description: Input-referred voltage noise density e_n, in V/sqrt(Hz) - the headline of low-noise matched pairs (MAT03, SSM2212). Same name and unit as AAS amplifierCommon.voltageNoiseDensity, so one query covers op amps and matched transistors. Typical column.

voltageNoiseDensityFrequency.description: Frequency at which voltageNoiseDensity is specified, in Hz (the AAS name).

voltageNoiseDensityCollectorCurrent.description: Collector current at which voltageNoiseDensity is specified, in A. A BJT's e_n depends strongly on I_C (shot noise falls, r_bb' noise stays), so the figure carries its bias condition.

biasResistors.description: Built-in bias resistors of a resistor-equipped ('pre-biased', 'digital') transistor. Present only on such a transistor; see bjtBiasResistors.

inputOnVoltage.description: On-state input voltage V_I(on): the input-to-ground (base-terminal-to-emitter, through R1) voltage at which the transistor carries inputOnVoltageIc at inputOnVoltageVce, in V, as a magnitude. Stored as the DISTRIBUTION of that voltage: minimum/nominal/maximum bound the voltage at which the stated current is reached, so the drive that guarantees 'on' is the maximum. Vendors print it two ways and both map here without arithmetic: Toshiba prints the distribution itself (min..max, stored as is); Nexperia and ROHM print the guarantee as a 'Min' column ('V_I(on) min 2.5 V' = on for any input >= 2.5 V), which is the distribution's maximum.

inputOnVoltageVce.description: Collector-emitter voltage at which inputOnVoltage is specified, in V (magnitude).

inputOnVoltageIc.description: Collector (output) current at which inputOnVoltage is specified, in A (magnitude).

inputOffVoltage.description: Off-state input voltage V_I(off): the input voltage at which the collector current falls to inputOffVoltageIc at inputOffVoltageVce, in V, as a magnitude. Stored as the DISTRIBUTION of that voltage (see inputOnVoltage), so the input level that guarantees 'off' is the minimum. Toshiba prints the distribution (stored as is); Nexperia and ROHM print the guarantee as a 'Max' column ('V_I(off) max 0.8 V' = off for any input <= 0.8 V), which is the distribution's minimum.

inputOffVoltageVce.description: Collector-emitter voltage at which inputOffVoltage is specified, in V (magnitude).

inputOffVoltageIc.description: Collector (output) current at which inputOffVoltage is specified, in A (magnitude).

inputVoltageMax.description: Absolute maximum forward input voltage, input terminal to ground, in V (Nexperia V_I 'positive', onsemi V_IN(fwd), ROHM V_IN upper limit), as a magnitude.

inputReverseVoltageMax.description: Absolute maximum reverse input voltage, in V, as a magnitude (Nexperia V_I 'negative' -10 V is stored as 10; onsemi V_IN(rev)).

outputCurrentMax.description: Rated output current I_O, in A, ONLY where the datasheet prints it separately from, and lower than, the built-in transistor's I_C(max) (ROHM: I_O 50 mA beside I_C(MAX) 100 mA). Where I_O is the part's only current rating (Nexperia 'I_O output current'), it is collectorCurrent and this field is omitted.

die.title: bjtDie
die.description: One transistor die inside a multi-die BJT package (dual, complementary pair, matched pair, quad or larger array), with the complete BJT electrical block the single-device file already defines: the same physics and the same field names as a single-die part, stated once per die. Every die states its own values even when the datasheet prints them once for 'each transistor', so 'both transistors are 45 V' and 'the part is 45 V' are different documents. powerDissipation inside a die is the PER-TRANSISTOR rating; a package total is not a die figure and is never divided down to fill this slot (it goes in datasheetInfo.packagePowerDissipation).

subType.description: Polarity OF THIS DIE. A complementary pair has one npn die and one pnp die in one part; the single-device part.subType cannot say that.

electrical.description: The complete BJT electrical block, per die (same definition and same required V_CEO + I_C as a single-die part).

thermal.description: Per-die thermal figures where the datasheet gives them. The package figure stays in datasheetInfo.thermal.

matching.title: bjtMatching
matching.description: One matching specification between die of a multi-die BJT: how closely the named transistors agree, at the stated test conditions. Matching is a property of a PAIR (or set) of die, never of one die, so it sits beside dies[] rather than inside a die. Each quantity is a dimensionWithTolerance so the datasheet's typical (nominal) and guaranteed (maximum) columns are both kept; magnitudes are absolute values.

dies.description: Names (dies[].name) of the die this specification relates. Absent means it holds between ANY two die of the part, which is how quad datasheets state it. The schema cannot check that the names exist in dies[]; that is the ingest gate's job.

baseEmitterVoltageMatch.description: |Delta V_BE| between the die at equal collector current - the offset voltage V_OS of the pair, in V.

baseEmitterVoltageMatchDrift.description: Temperature drift of the V_BE match (offset-voltage tracking, TCV_OS), in V/K.

currentGainMatch.description: Current-gain match |Delta h_FE| / h_FE as a fraction (0.005 = 0.5%).

baseCurrentMatch.description: Base-current match |I_B1 - I_B2| (input offset current I_OS of the pair), in A.

collectorCurrentMatch.description: Collector-current match |I_C1/I_C2 - 1| as a fraction - the mirror-ratio error of a current-mirror pair (BCV61/62, BCM61/62).

testCollectorCurrent.description: Collector current per die at which the matching is specified, in A.

testCollectorBaseVoltage.description: Collector-base voltage at which the matching is specified, in V.

testTemperature.description: Ambient temperature at which the matching is specified, in degC.

biasResistors.title: bjtBiasResistors
biasResistors.description: The bias-resistor network built into a resistor-equipped transistor (a 'pre-biased', 'digital', BRT or RET part): R1 in series with the base (the input resistor) and R2 from base to emitter. Its presence is what marks a transistor as pre-biased; a plain transistor omits it, and no separate flag exists that could contradict it. One block per transistor: on a multi-die part it sits in each dies[].electrical, because the two transistors of a pair may carry different resistors. R2 'open' (R1-only types such as PDTC114T, RN1711JE) is stated by omitting baseEmitterResistance, never by a sentinel value. Each resistance is a dimensionWithTolerance in Ohm: nominal = the datasheet's typical (or title) value, minimum/maximum = its limits. A tolerance printed as a percentage (Panasonic '-30% 22 +30%') is stored as the limits it states.

baseResistance.description: R1, the series base (input) resistor, in Ohm.

baseEmitterResistance.description: R2, the base-emitter resistor, in Ohm. Datasheets usually print only its nominal (in the title or a type table) and toleranced R1 plus the ratio; store what is printed and do not derive R2 limits from R1 and the ratio.

resistanceRatio.description: The resistor ratio exactly as printed, in the direction resistanceRatioDefinition names (dimensionless). Vendors disagree on the direction: Nexperia and ROHM print R2/R1; onsemi, Toshiba and Panasonic print R1/R2. The value is stored as printed and never inverted.
